english_translation: A light-complexioned woman looks downward; her blonde-dyed hair is closely trimmed on the sides with a parted line and fuller textured curls on top.

dialogue.shona: Munhukadzi mutsvuku akatsikitsira. Ane musoro une vhudzi jena rakagerwa nechekumativi pakaiswa mutaro. Pamusoro pane vhudzi rakakuririra rakabvanyangurwa.
dialogue.english: A woman is looking downward; her light-coloured hair is trimmed on the sides with a part line and fuller styled hair on top.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Munhukadzi [in / singular nhukadzi] • mutsvuku [in / singular tsvuku] • akatsikitsira [he/she (past) tsikitsira] • Ane [ane] • musoro [in / singular soro] • une [une] • vhudzi [vhudzi] • jena [jena]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('akatsikitsira')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'akatsikitsira' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Colours & Describing Objects in Shona ('mutsvuku')
grammar_notes.content: This passage uses colour vocabulary such as 'mutsvuku'. Shona has three traditional core colour adjectives that change their prefix slightly to match the noun they describe: '-chena' (white/clean, e.g., 'ruvara ruchena' or 'shangu chena'), '-tema / nhema' (black/dark, e.g., 'mota nhema' or 'ruvara rutema'), and '-tsvuku' (red/bright brown, e.g., 'mota tsvuku' or 'ruvara rutsvuku'). For other colours like green ('girinhi'), blue ('bhuruu'), or orange ('orenji'), speakers typically say 'ruvara rwe-' ('the colour of...') followed by the colour name, as in 'ruvara rwegirinhi' (green).
grammar_notes.rule: Core Colours: -chena (white), -tema / nhema (black), -tsvuku (red) | Phrase pattern: ruvara rwe-[colour] (e.g., ruvara rwegirinhi)

grammar_notes.title: Talking About Location: 'pa-', 'ku-', and 'mu-' ('Pamusoro')
grammar_notes.content:
Look at how location is expressed with 'Pamusoro'. Instead of separate prepositions like 'on', 'to', or 'in', Shona attaches one of three location prefixes directly to the front of a noun:
• 'pa-' means 'at' or 'on' a specific point or surface (e.g., 'patafura' = on the table, 'pamusika' = at the market, 'pasi' = on the ground).
• 'ku-' means 'to', 'from', or 'at' a general destination (e.g., 'kuchikoro' = to school, 'kumusha' = to the rural home, 'kubasa' = at/to work).
• 'mu-' means 'inside' an enclosed space (e.g., 'mumba' = inside the house, 'muguta' = in the city, 'mumugwagwa' = in the road).
grammar_notes.rule: pa- = on / at a point (patafura) | ku- = to / at a place (kuchikoro) | mu- = inside (mumba)

cultural_notes.title: Contemporary Salon Barbering & Hair Colouring ('Mutaro & Vhudzi Jena')
cultural_notes.content: Modern Zimbabwean hair salons blend precision barbering—such as tapered sides with a razor-sharp part line ('mutaro')—with bold blonde and honey-toned hair colouring ('vhudzi jena').
